done_when: SUPER_SESSION.md gets a short 'Pacing checklist' section (reusing Rule 5's remaining-minutes/40 heuristic, no new script, no scheduler) that a coordinator runs on every wake: get_usage, and when the 5h window or its own turn/context budget is close to its limit, hand off live to a fresh coordinator (D5/D6) instead of idling or stopping. One worked example (2026-10-27 chain, NEXT_SESSION.md numbers) cited. turn_meter.py coordinator-distinction question resolved (the hook no longer exists) and noted in the result, not fixed in code.
goal: Operator priority-1 request (2026-10-27, this session): coordinators should 'keep rolling' -- pace real dispatched work so a super-session chain uses up its usage window without a coordinator dying early (handing off while there is still budget and ready backlog) or overrunning (grinding turns with no real task once budget/backlog is spent). Keep it simple: no new scheduler, no new service -- extend the existing rule 12 heuristic and rule 5 hand-off into one explicit checklist in SUPER_SESSION.md.
note: Context: operator asked this session (local_37a9ec3e) to 'exhaust the session' as a pacing test, then clarified the real ask is a standing MTS capability -- a rolling coordinator chain that self-paces to the usage window, simply. This session observed a real mismatch worth fixing as part of this card: turn_meter.py's generic single-task cap (CLAUDE.md step 5, ~10 operator/40 tool turns) fires on coordinator sessions too, even though SUPER_SESSION.md rule 9 says Sonnet/Haiku coordinators get a much larger context-based cap (4M/context tokens) and are meant to run for hours. Whoever refines this card should check whether turn_meter.py already distinguishes coordinator sessions, and if not, whether that belongs in this card or a separate one.
result: Added '## Pacing checklist (every wake)' to SUPER_SESSION.md (after Rules, before Mechanics): get_usage every wake; hand off LIVE to a fresh coordinator when the 5h window nears D6's 80% stop or context nears the ~200K D5 rotation point, reusing Rule 5's remaining-minutes/40 arithmetic as the hand-off trigger (no new formula, no scheduler). Cited worked example: 2026-10-27 DESKTOP-F7IU69N chain wound down at 94% of its 5h window (~1h6m left, weekly 40%, context ~12%), per NEXT_SESSION.md. Rule number note: the card's 'rule 9'/'rule 12'/'rule 5' citations are pre-2026-10-24-redesign numbers (file went 137->73 lines that day); mapped here to current Rule 5 (Spend the window), D5 (rotation) and D6 (stop conditions), and the Mechanics 'Turn caps' bullet. turn_meter.py check: it does NOT distinguish coordinator sessions because it (and model_guard.py) were removed from trunk entirely on 2026-10-24 (43d3bfc8f) and are absent from .claude/settings.json -- no hook enforces any turn/tool cap on any session today, so the mismatch the card worried about no longer exists as stated. Not fixed in code (out of scope, and nothing to fix: the file is gone). Doc tests pass: test_integrity.py (15), test_super_session_doc.py (7).

title: Coordinator self-pacing: rolling super-session chain exhausts the usage window without dying early or overrunning
